stories.headline: Phone prices just had a record jump.
stories.body: US prices rose <mark>0.4% in October</mark>, more than expected. <mark>Smartphones</mark> had their <mark>biggest monthly rise on record</mark>, TVs jumped too, and <mark>groceries</mark> rose the most in <mark>six months</mark>. Markets now bet the Fed may <mark>raise rates</mark>.

stories.headline: Meta launched its cheapest AI model yet.
stories.body: <mark>Muse Ember</mark> costs <mark>$0.10 per million input tokens</mark> and $0.50 for output, with a <mark>1M-token</mark> context window. It's built for the <mark>repetitive steps AI agents do all day</mark>. Meta claims it beats rivals on value, but that's <mark>Meta's own claim</mark>.

stories.headline: A message to Voyager 1 now takes a full day.
stories.body: On <mark>Nov 18</mark>, Voyager 1 hits <mark>one light-day</mark> from Earth, about <mark>25.9 billion km</mark>. Launched in <mark>1977</mark>, it's the first spacecraft to get that far. A signal needs <mark>24 hours</mark> to reach it, and <mark>another 24</mark> to hear back.

stories.headline: NASA picked 8 companies for Moon deliveries.
stories.body: <mark>SpaceX, Blue Origin</mark> and six others can now bid on <mark>lunar delivery missions</mark> under a <mark>10-year contract</mark> worth up to <mark>$10 billion</mark>. That's a <mark>ceiling, not money spent yet</mark>. Blue Origin also got <mark>$94M</mark> to land a <mark>nuclear-powered rover</mark>.
